brief: GS's Privorotsky argues capital scarcity, not earnings, is now the market's binding constraint: post-GFC fiscal deficits and entitlement spending assumed permanently cheap capital, but sovereign financing needs plus AI's compute buildout (SpaceX reportedly seeking $40bn, Broadcom $50bn+) are crowding out consumers, small businesses and governments, which he says helps explain why real yields won't fall. He frames the resolution as two paths: AI cash flow turns self-financing, making the next round of hyperscaler earnings pivotal, or capital gets rationed elsewhere and weak credits break first, a stress he says may already show in CCC spreads. Against this, Samsung (₩107.4tn operating profit) and TSMC (Q3 sales +50% YoY) both beat, yet Asian equities fell anyway; LG's miss despite revenue growth is the more telling non-AI read. Oil jumped on a tanker strike off Qatar, raising Hormuz-contagion risk with no credible political off-ramp before the midterms. The 10yr auction (2.77x cover) went well but long-end vol stays elevated. He stays constructive on AI, calling the Russell's 17-of-20-session underperformance versus the Nasdaq rational given the backdrop, but is unsure what resolves European sovereign stress.
